name: Uzza
overview: Uzza is a male figure known primarily as the owner of the garden where Manasseh was buried, as recorded in 2 Kings 21:18. There is no tribal affiliation or additional personal information provided about him in Scripture. His mention is brief and specific to this unique attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzza is a proper name meaning "strong, fierce one." This meaning reflects a characteristic implied in the name but is not explicitly connected to his actions or role in the biblical text. The name was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Uzza beyond his ownership of the garden where Manasseh was buried. There are no additional relational details provided.
scriptureSignificance: Uzza's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his ownership of the garden where Manasseh, a king of Judah, was buried. This connection places Uzza in the historical and geographical context of Judah's royal history, though he himself remains a minor figure. His mention helps to situate the burial of Manasseh within a known location, contributing to the historical record in Scripture.
